persona.purpose: Find fellowships, funding deadlines and maybe people outside her lab — on her laptop between experiments.
persona.backstory: I live in my lab. I'd like to know about fellowships and travel grants before the deadline instead of hearing about them a week late, and honestly it would be nice to meet people who aren't in my research group. I'm allergic to apps that treat me like an undergrad.
quitsWhen: Mobile-only layout stretched on my laptop
persona.voice: Precise, a little dry. Notices sloppy details. 'This deadline is wrong', 'Why is this here?'

scenario.title: Find an internship near Berkeley
scenario.goal: You need a paid internship (summer or part-time) somewhere near Berkeley / the Bay Area. Use the app to find one that looks real and open, and open its details so you know how to apply.

success.description: An internship listing's detail page is open (reached by the persona — the run starts on /).

environment.summary: Local stack: this worktree's server + built web app, fresh seeded FileStore per run, no secrets, no worker.
knownLimits: Dining menus and RSF gym crowd levels need live campus sources (the local stack runs with CAMPUS_LIVE=0) — empty or missing data there is not a UX bug.
AI features (Ask Lumi, AI profile draft on /start, conversation starters) need an OpenAI key; none is configured locally.
Course catalog is the real Berkeley Class Schedule (6588 courses, Fall 2026 + Spring 2027), fetched 2026-11-02 with the worker's adapter. Seat counts and very recent changes may differ from live.

Campus events, free food, internships, hackathons and scholarships are a read-only snapshot of live (1119 real items, 103 events this week, taken 2026-11-02 07:25 UTC) plus the CSV calendar. Nothing new appears during the run; Q&A and reviews are empty.
No e-mail is sent: the sign-up / sign-in code is shown on screen in the hint (live sends a real e-mail).
Real-time updates (SSE) work locally; other people never reply unless the stack was started with --autoreply.

Signed in as a brand-new real (non-sample, e-mail-verified) account made for this run. Other students exist only if the scenario seeds peers (local fixtures); sample profiles are hidden from real accounts, as on live.

frictionEvents.quote: A phone-sized column in the middle of my 1440px screen, with a note telling me to go use my phone. At least it's not stretched. Free food feed is very undergrad, but fine, I'm here for internships.
frictionEvents.wish: a real desktop layout, or at least don't tell me to switch devices

frictionEvents.quote: 'Invite your floor' — I don't have a floor, I have a lab. This is a dorm app. Maybe 'Browse' hides something useful.
frictionEvents.wish: a visible Jobs/Internships or Opportunities entry point

frictionEvents.quote: Okay, this is actually relevant — 'PhD' intern roles, a Jane Street grad fellowship. Should not be buried under a tab labelled 'Browse' inside 'Campus' though. And the old feed lingered for a moment after I clicked.
frictionEvents.wish: label it Opportunities, or surface it from the home screen

frictionEvents.quote: Wall of chips — 'Health 0' is a chip for nothing. But there's a location filter, which is exactly what I need. The dropdown hanging off the edge of the column is sloppy.
frictionEvents.wish: keep the dropdown inside the layout; hide zero-count chips

frictionEvents.quote: Why is 'Prep crews' above the job details? I wanted location/pay/deadline first. No compensation listed at all — I'll assume Waymo pays its PhD interns, but the app should say so. The deadline note is at least honest.
frictionEvents.wish: show compensation (or 'paid') and put details above the social stuff

outcomeReason: Found a Waymo MS/PhD summer intern role in Mountain View, verified from the official source on Nov 1, with an Apply on Waymo link. Pay isn't stated, which is sloppy, but it's clearly a real, open posting.

successCheck.evaluatedFrom: first persona action (never the start screen)

dropoffRisk.rationale: The opportunities board is genuinely useful for a PhD (PhD-level roles, fellowships, Bay Area filter), but it's hidden behind Campus > Browse under a dorm-style social feed, and the detail page leads with prep crews instead of pay/details. I'd come back only if I bookmarked the board directly.
